previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient was admitted with right lower quadrant abdominal pain and subjective fevers two weeks after a laparoscopic appendectomy. Imaging revealed a periappendiceal abscess, which was successfully drained percutaneously under CT guidance. She was managed with intravenous fluids, pain control, and transitioned to oral antibiotics and analgesics. Her white blood cell count improved, she tolerated a regular diet, and was ambulating independently at discharge. She was discharged home with a 10-day course of ciprofloxacin and metronidazole, instructions to avoid heavy lifting for six weeks, and a follow-up appointment in two weeks for repeat imaging. Her mood and mental status remained stable throughout the admission.

radiology_notes.text:
CLINICAL INDICATION:  Left lower quadrant intermittent pain.  Evaluate for
torsion.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale, color and spectral Doppler ultrasound evaluation of the
pelvis via a transabdominal approach and subsequently via a transvaginal
approach for better delineation of anatomy.

COMPARISON:  Pelvic ultrasound ___.

FINDINGS:  The uterus measures 6.1 x 2.2 x 3.7 cm.  The endometrium is
homogeneous.  The right ovary contains a 2-cm simple cyst.  Both ovaries
appear normal and demonstrate normal arterial and venous waveforms.  No free
fluid is identified.

IMPRESSION:  Normal-appearing uterus and ovaries.  Arterial and venous
waveforms demonstrated in both ovaries.
